subject: general
question: A hemispherical solid of radius 21 cm is melted and made into a cylinder whose height is 14 cm. The volume of the cylinder is given by (a x ba x cb)π where a, b and c are prime. Then the value of (a+b)c is
solution:
**Given:**

Radius of hemisphere = 21 cm

Height of cylinder = 14 cm

**Formula used:**

Volume of hemisphere = (2/3) × π × r³

Volume of cylinder = π × r² × h

**Calculation:**

Volume of hemisphere = (2/3) × π × 21³

This volume is converted into a cylinder of height 14 cm

Volume of cylinder = π × r² × 14 = π × r² × 14

Equating both:

(2/3) × π × 213 = π × r² × 14

(2/3) × 213 = r2 × 14

⇒ r = 21

We are given that the volume is (a × ba × cb)

Calculate actual volume of cylinder = π × 212 × 14

After factors we get,

Volume of cylinder = π (2 × 3² × 7³)

On comparing by (a x ba x cb)π, we get;

So, a = 2, b = 3, c = 7

(a + b)c = (2 + 3)5 = 35

**∴ The value of (a + b)c = 35**
